findings.rationale: FL's uploaded updates are about 12x the median norm in every round from round 1 (median norm ratio 11.86, z=+13.4), and the cosine to the median update is near zero and changes sign between rounds (round 1 cos -0.15, round 7 cos -0.14, round 20 cos +0.25), with mean cos 0.095. That pattern fits large random noise added to uploads rather than a consistent sign-flip. Its local performance is normal (AUC 0.810, CITL -0.011), so accuracy is not visibly harmed.

NY's updates are about 12.6x the median norm (z=+12.6), with mean cos 0.10 and cosine swinging between negative and positive values across rounds (round 2 -0.095, round 4 +0.70, round 8 -0.24). The pattern is consistent with large random noise in the uploads. Local AUC is normal (0.854) and CITL is near zero.

UT's updates are about 11.9x the median norm (z=+14.0) in every round, with mean cos 0.19 and cosine oscillating in sign across rounds (round 1 -0.06, round 10 +0.58, round 19 -0.21). The large, non-directional deviations match random upload noise. Local AUC is normal (0.835).

Weak-to-moderate lead. GU's observed outcome prevalence (0.201) is well above what its features predict (mean predicted 0.142), giving the most negative CITL of any client at round 20. Its AUC is normal (0.888). Drift CITL is also strongly negative at both first and last round (-0.27 and -0.38). A repeat Sex subgroup query shows observed/expected of about 1.5-1.75 in both sex groups, i.e. a client-wide prevalence excess rather than under-recording in one subgroup. GU is small (n_train 708, test 237), so this is treated as a lead, not a confirmed finding.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of the update, performance, drift, feature and subgroup tools, then confirmed leads with narrower queries. The clearest signal is three clients (FL, NY, UT) whose uploads are about 12x the median norm from round 1, with near-zero, sign-changing cosine to the median and normal local AUC. That pattern fits random upload noise (explanation_instability) rather than a directed sign-flip poisoning, so I flagged all three at onset round 1 with moderate confidence. GU is a weaker prevalence_shift lead (observed prevalence above predicted, normal AUC, persistent negative CITL) with lower confidence. Other outliers (NC GenHlth, ND HighChol, WV Income subgroup, DC drift, WI, AL, PR, GU update norm) did not persist on re-query or were within noise, so I did not report them. The privacy budget is fully spent.
